treks.shortDescription: The classic Himalayan journey through high Sherpa villages, ancient pine forests, and dramatic glacial moraines to the foot of Mount Everest.
treks.overview: Our Everest Base Camp journey is carefully paced with two dedicated acclimatisation days in Namche Bazaar and Dingboche, prioritising your safety, comfort, and connection with Sherpa heritage. Stand beneath the towering south face of Nuptse and gaze across the Khumbu Icefall.

treks.acclimatisationPlan: Designed according to international wilderness medical protocols: gradual ascent, active rest hikes on rest days (Hotel Everest View 3,880m and Nangkartshang Peak 5,083m), and conservative sleeping elevation gains.

faqs.question: How fit do I need to be for Everest Base Camp?
faqs.answer: A good level of aerobic fitness and endurance is recommended. You should be comfortable walking 5 to 7 hours daily with a light daypack across uneven terrain.

faqs.question: What happens in case of altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: Our guides monitor your pulse and oxygen saturation daily. If severe symptoms occur, immediate descent is initiated, and helicopter evacuation is coordinated 24/7 with Kathmandu desk.

Summit of Gokyo Ri with panoramas of four 8,000-metre peaks

treks.overview: For experienced adventurers seeking true wilderness. After exploring Langtang Valley, leave the teahouses behind to camp on snowfields, cross the narrow knife-edge gap of Ganja La Pass (5,130m) with fixed ropes, and emerge into remote high pastures.
highlights: Technical alpine crossing of Ganja La Pass (5,130m)
True expedition camping in high glaciated basins
Incredible close-up views of Langtang Lirung and Shishapangma in Tibet
Descent into untouched Helambu villages
treks.acclimatisationPlan: Acclimatise thoroughly in Kyanjin Gompa with day hikes to 4,700m before entering the camping zone.

highlights: Conquering Larkya La Pass (5,160m) with views of Himlung and Annapurna II
Close-up views of Mount Manaslu (8,163m) from Birendra Lake
Ancient Buddhist monasteries in Samagaon and Samdo
Strictly preserved wilderness without roads or commercial sprawl
treks.acclimatisationPlan: Full rest day in Samagaon (3,530m) with acclimatisation hike to Manaslu Base Camp or Pungyen Gompa.

treks.title: Tsum Valley Sacred Hidden Sanctuary
treks.shortDescription: Discover the sacred "Beyul" hidden valley where Milarepa meditated, where animal slaughter is forbidden, and centuries of Buddhist peace thrive.
treks.overview: Tsum Valley was completely closed to foreigners until 2008. Revered as a sacred beyul (hidden sanctuary) blessed by Guru Rinpoche, it is a non-violent valley where no hunting or animal slaughter is allowed, filled with ancient cliff nunneries, chortens, and Mu Gompa.
highlights: Centuries-old Mu Gompa and Rachen Nunnery at 3,700m
Milarepa’s sacred meditation cave with footprint relics
Unique non-violent Buddhist valley culture (Ahimsa)
Spectacular views of Ganesh Himal and Sringi Himal
treks.acclimatisationPlan: Moderate maximum elevation of 3,700m makes it comfortable and deeply spiritual.

treks.shortDescription: Step through the gates of the ancient walled city of Lo Manthang in the mystical Tibetan rain-shadow canyon desert.

Mysterious ancient sky caves carved high into sheer canyon cliffs
Unique rain-shadow climate: sunny and dry during summer monsoon
Centuries-old Tibetan monasteries of Jampa and Thubchen Gompa

treks.title: Upper Dolpo & Shey Phoksundo Crystal Mountain Trek
treks.shortDescription: The land of the Snow Leopard: turquoise Shey Phoksundo lake, ancient Bon po monasteries, and high wild passes of the far west.
treks.overview: Immortalized in Peter Matthiessen’s "The Snow Leopard" and Eric Valli’s film "Himalaya", Upper Dolpo is Nepal’s most remote and authentic wilderness. Traverse high passes, gaze into the bottomless turquoise waters of Phoksundo Lake, and circle the Crystal Mountain at Shey Gompa.
highlights: Deep turquoise glacial waters of Shey Phoksundo Lake (3,611m)
800-year-old Shey Gompa beneath the sacred Crystal Mountain
Pre-Buddhist ancient Bon po monasteries and yak caravans
Complete isolation in Nepal’s largest national park

expeditions.overview: Himlung Himal rises gracefully above the ancient stone villages of Nar and Phu. Offering non-technical snow slopes without treacherous seracs, it is the ideal first 7,000-metre expedition for climbers aiming for higher peaks.

Trek through the restricted and mystical valleys of Nar and Phu
Non-technical glacial slopes with low objective avalanche danger

Senior elite Sherpa expedition crew with extensive high-altitude record

faqs.answer: Out of deep respect for the local Sikkimese and Sherpa religious beliefs that the summit is the home of deities, climbers stop a few feet below the crest.

Designed for mountaineers and ambitious trekkers with strong fitness seeking their first Himalayan 6,000m summit, our expedition features a comprehensive pre-climb training day at High Camp, low climber-to-Sherpa guide ratios (2:1 or 1:1), and fixed rope safety systems.

Acclimatisation via Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar prior to the climb
Professional IFMGA/NNMGA certified Sherpa climbing leaders
Hands-on ropework, crampon, and jumar training session at Base Camp

faqs.question: Is prior climbing experience needed?

expeditions.shortDescription: Technical granite slab scrambling and steep snow headwall leading to a breathtaking summit directly overlooking the Khumbu glacier.

highlights: Technical climbing up exposed snow slopes and granite slabs

expeditions.overview: Yala Peak is classified as a non-technical trekking peak that does not require expensive government peak royalties. Located just beyond Kyanjin Gompa in the Langtang Valley, it offers an authentic high-camp experience and summit vistas into Tibet.

expeditions.overview: Chulu West towers over the arid valley of Manang. A true mountaineering challenge, the ascent follows a glaciated northwest ridge requiring fixed rope handling, cramponing, and high camp positioning, with panoramic vistas of Annapurna II, III, IV, Gangapurna, and Dhaulagiri.
highlights: Summit of one of Nepal’s premier 6,400m alpine trekking peaks

Trek through the ancient Buddhist villages of Pisang and Manang

culturalProfile.title: Sacred Valleys & Living Sherpa Heritage
culturalProfile.narrative: The Khumbu is consecrated as a Beyul—a sacred hidden valley sanctified by Guru Rinpoche in the 8th century. The Sherpa people migrated from eastern Tibet over five centuries ago, bringing resilient Buddhist traditions that still govern daily life. Every trail is woven with carved Mani stone walls (which travelers must pass on the left), spinning prayer wheels, and chortens blessed by senior Rinpoches.
traditions: Mani Rimdu sacred masked dance festival (Autumn)
Sustainable yak pastoralism and potato terraces

faqs.question: How physically demanding is travelling in the Everest region?
faqs.answer: Trails are well-engineered stone paths with gradual switchbacks, but sustained altitude gain requires good aerobic stamina. Trekkers should be comfortable walking 5 to 7 hours daily with a light daypack. Dedicated acclimatisation days in Namche and Dingboche are mandatory in our itineraries.

faqs.question: What happens if flights to Lukla are delayed by weather?
faqs.answer: Lukla flights rely on visual flight rules (VFR). When cloud cover closes the runway, EcoSummit provides immediate priority access to commercial helicopter charters and includes built-in buffer days in Kathmandu to safeguard international flight connections.

faqs.question: Can I do a shorter trip in Khumbu if I don’t have 14 days?
faqs.answer: Yes! The Everest Panorama Trek (7–9 days to Tengboche) offers stunning views of Everest, Ama Dablam, and Lhotse without going beyond 3,867m. We also offer luxury helicopter day dispatches to Hotel Everest View.

faqs.question: What are accommodation standards like in the Khumbu?
faqs.answer: Lower Khumbu offers luxury boutique lodges (Yeti Mountain Home, Everest Summit Lodges) with heated electric blankets, en-suite bathrooms, and fine dining. High valley teahouses provide clean private twin rooms with communal heated dining halls.

faqs.question: Does EcoSummit manage all permits and fees beforehand?
faqs.answer: Yes. All national park permits, local municipality cards, guide credentials, and emergency helicopter rescue insurance clearances are pre-arranged before you depart Kathmandu.

wildlifeEcology.conservationNote: Protected heritage zones overseen by the Department of Archaeology and UNESCO.

faqs.question: How many days do you recommend in Kathmandu?
faqs.answer: We recommend at least 2 to 3 days to explore the three historic royal cities (Kathmandu, Patan, Bhaktapur) and stay overnight on the scenic rim in Nagarkot or Dhulikhel.

destinations.name: Pokhara & Phewa Lake
destinations.subtitle: The Gateway to the Annapurnas
destinations.description: A tranquil lakeside haven reflecting the fish-tail pinnacle of Machapuchare, surrounded by organic coffee hills, peaceful stupas, and forest viewpoints.
destinations.unescoStatus: Phewa Lake Ramsar Wetland Site Candidate
destinations.dominantCulture: Gurung, Magar and Newar lakeside communities
destinations.trailStyle: Lakeside Promenades, Ridge Trails & Forested Sanctuary Walks
highlights: Watching golden dawn sunlight illuminate Machapuchare from Sarangkot
Paddling hand-crafted wooden boats on the calm mirror waters of Phewa Lake
Visiting the white dome of the World Peace Pagoda on the forested ridge
Relaxing in boutique spa resorts with farm-to-table Himalayan dining

culturalProfile.title: Lakeside Serenity Under the Holy Summit
culturalProfile.narrative: Pokhara is Nepal’s premier relaxation haven, situated 820m above sea level with dramatic 8,000m mountains rising just 28 km north—creating the steepest vertical elevation gain anywhere on Earth.
traditions: Lakeside artistic culture, organic coffee farming in the hills

landmarksList.name: Phewa Lake & Tal Barahi Temple
landmarksList.description: Tranquil freshwater lake with a two-story island temple.

permits: No permits required for general Pokhara city and lakeside stays
permitsLogistics.weatherNote: Warm subtropical daytime temperatures, pleasant evenings year-round.
permitsLogistics.flightLogistics: 25-minute domestic flights operate every 30 minutes between Kathmandu and Pokhara.

flora: Subtropical sal forests, wild orchids and tea plantations
fauna: Migratory waterbirds, otters, kingfishers and butterflies
wildlifeEcology.conservationNote: Wetland preservation projects protecting the Phewa watershed.

faqs.question: Is Pokhara included before and after Annapurna treks?
faqs.answer: Yes! All our Annapurna journeys include luxury lodge stays in Pokhara to rest and unwind before and after your trek.

destinations.name: Chitwan & Terai Jungles
destinations.subtitle: Wild Terai Forests & Subtropical Wildlife
destinations.description: The green subtropical plains of southern Nepal, where greater one-horned rhinoceroses, Royal Bengal tigers, gharial crocodiles, and over 500 bird species thrive.
destinations.unescoStatus: Chitwan National Park UNESCO Natural World Heritage Site (Inscribed 1984)
destinations.trailStyle: River Boat Safaris, Jungle Walks & 4WD Open Jeep Tracks
highlights: Encountering wild one-horned rhinos grazing peacefully in the tall elephant grass
Quiet wooden canoe safari on the Rapti River observing basking gharial crocodiles
Tracking elusive Royal Bengal Tigers with veteran local naturalists
Staying at sustainable luxury eco-lodges along the tranquil riverbanks
destinations.bestSeason: October–March (Pleasant dry winter, tall grass burned for peak wildlife viewing)
keyPeaks: Lowland subtropical plains beneath the Siwalik Hills

culturalProfile.title: Indigenous Tharu Culture & River Wisdom
culturalProfile.narrative: The Tharu people have lived in the malarial Terai jungles for centuries, developing natural genetic immunity and an intimate knowledge of forest medicine, animal behavior, and mud-and-thatch architecture decorated with tribal animal motifs.
traditions: Traditional net fishing in dugout canoes

landmarksList.name: Rapti River Waterfront
landmarksList.description: Prime sunset spot where wild rhinos and deer emerge to drink.

permits: Chitwan National Park Entry Permit (NPR 2,000 / day, handled by EcoSummit)
permitsLogistics.weatherNote: Tropical jungle climate; warm during days, cool mist over the river at dawn.
permitsLogistics.flightLogistics: Daily 20-minute flights from Kathmandu to Bharatpur followed by luxury private transfer.

flora: Sal tree forests (Shorea robusta), riverine silk cotton and elephant grass
wildlifeEcology.conservationNote: Global conservation success story with zero-poaching years and thriving rhino populations.

faqs.question: Does EcoSummit support ethical wildlife tourism in Chitwan?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100%. We strictly prohibit elephant riding and only conduct non-invasive walking safaris, solar-powered boat floats, and 4WD open jeep safaris led by licensed senior naturalists.

reviews.name: Dr. Markus Weber
reviews.title: Authentic Himalayan expedition without commercial hype
reviews.content: The logistics for Manaslu are notoriously tricky due to restricted permits and high pass weather windows. Dawa and the EcoSummit Kathmandu office managed every detail seamlessly. The village stays in Samdo and Sama Gaun felt deeply genuine. An authentic Himalayan mountain journey without any commercial hype.

reviews.name: Elena Rostova & David Miller
reviews.title: Extraordinary private circuit with helicopter views
reviews.content: Traveling with elderly parents required careful pacing and zero steep climbs. EcoSummit tailored an extraordinary 8-day private luxury circuit with helicopter mountain views, private heritage scholars in Bhaktapur, and peaceful mornings in Pokhara. Simply flawless hospitality.

reviews.name: Karma_De (Mindful Trekker)
reviews.title: Exceeded all expectations from beginning to end
reviews.content: My Annapurna Base Camp trek with EcoSummit was an excellent experience from beginning to end. Transparent pricing, top-tier pulse oximeter monitoring each morning, and guides who treat the mountains with utmost respect. 5 stars all around!

reviews.name: Alvaro Gomez
reviews.title: Professional mountain team with unmatched local safety
reviews.content: Estuve con el equipo de EcoSummit haciendo el trekking de los Tres Pasos de Everest. Fue una experiencia inolvidable. Los guías conocen cada roca del sendero y las casas de té donde dormimos fueron las mejores de la ruta. Muy profesionales y recomendables.

reviews.name: Cristina Muzzini
reviews.journey: Upper Mustang Kingdom of Lo Trek
reviews.title: Great trekking group, well organized and very caring guides
reviews.content: Traveling into the forbidden Kingdom of Lo was a dream. EcoSummit handled the special permits, private 4x4 transfers, and assigned us an elder Mustang native guide whose family has lived there for generations. Simply magical!

reviews.name: Infinix Sunrise Travel Notes
reviews.title: I recently completed Langtang Trek with EcoSummit, very satisfied!
reviews.content: I recently completed the Langtang Trek organized by EcoSummit and Tours, and I am very satisfied with the service. The porter-to-guest ratio was ethical, food was fresh and plentiful, and the team provided warm sleeping bags for high altitudes.

reviews.name: Julian & Claire Henderson
reviews.journey: Everest Base Camp & Kala Patthar (Private Journey)
reviews.title: A trip of a lifetime A huge thank you to EcoSummit
reviews.content: What distinguished EcoSummit was their calm, unhurried approach to acclimatisation. While other large commercial groups seemed rushed and stressed, our guide Pasang monitored our pacing daily with quiet expertise. Reaching Kala Patthar at sunrise with just our private party was one of the most sublime moments of our lives.

reviews.name: Sarah & Liam Connolly
reviews.title: Flawless safety and warm Himalayan hospitality
reviews.content: As first-time visitors to Nepal, we were anxious about logistics, food hygiene, and trail difficulty. EcoSummit balanced the adventure of walking into the high sanctuary bowl with comfortable lodge arrangements and warm, attentive care. We cannot recommend their local team highly enough.

reviews.name: theellacotts (Charlotte & Ben)
reviews.title: Excellent guide and wonderful experience trekking in the Himalayas
reviews.content: My husband and I had the most amazing experience trekking Langtang Valley. Our guide Pemba was attentive to every detail — from dietary needs to pacing on frozen stone ascents. The sunrise over Gosaikunda Lake surrounded by snowpeaks was breathtaking. Outstanding local operator.

reviews.name: kabiraj ghimire
reviews.title: Incredible Mardi Himal Trek as a solo traveler
reviews.content: Incredible Mardi Himal Trek with EcoSummit. As a solo traveler joining a private guide, I felt safe, cared for, and deeply immersed in the Sherpa and Gurung cultures. Standing on the high ridge facing Machapuchare (Fishtail) at 4,500m was surreal.

reviews.name: Tourist31712277035
reviews.journey: Everest Base Camp + Island Peak Climb
reviews.title: A trip of a lifetime planning our Everest Base Camp + Island Peak
reviews.content: Meticulously planned from arrival in Kathmandu to summiting Island Peak at 6,189m. Our climbing Sherpa was a 7-time Everest summiteer who inspected our ropes, crampons, and oxygen safety daily. World-class expertise.

reviews.name: 俊佐 吳 (Chun-Tso Wu)
reviews.journey: Everest Base Camp & Gokyo Lakes Helicopter Return
reviews.title: 值得推薦的旅行社 感謝團隊成功帶領我們完成環線
reviews.content: 值得推薦的旅行社！感謝團隊成功帶領我們完成島峰和EBC。團隊非常專業，甚至在我們班機延誤時在機場等待我們四個小時，當下真的很暖心！感謝有你們！
